transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood CSM); Mark Elliot (CISO, Suncrest), Lara Chen (Infra Lead), Daniel Ortiz (SecEng)

Summary:
High-level review of Redwood's BCDR / incident response processes, RTO/RPO targets, SLA uptime guarantees and escalation paths. Suncrest focused on auditability, KMS key ownership options, SSO/RBAC integration, and proving RTO/RPO via a short benchmark on Dedicated capacity. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC2/ISO artifacts, scheduling a deeper technical session, and provisioning a short trial for runbook validation.

Topics:
- Incident response timing and playbooks
- BCDR: RTO / RPO for hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- SLA uptime, credits, and support tiers
- Escalation process and on-call rotations
- Audit logs, retention, and tamper-evidence
- Encryption options (customer KMS/HSM) and key ownership
- SSO/SCIM/RBAC controls and integration cadence

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? Alex Moran here from Redwood, AE.
[00:06] Mark (Suncrest): Mark Elliot, CISO. Good afternoon.
[00:08] Lara: Lara Chen, infra.
[00:10] Daniel: Daniel Ortiz, security engineering.
[00:12] Priya (Redwood): Priya Shah, solutions engineer. Samir from CSM is also on.
[00:18] Samir (Redwood): Hey all.
[00:20] Alex: Great. Agenda is BCDR and incident response - RTO/RPO expectations, SLA and escalation. We'll try to leave time for questions.

[00:35] Mark: Topline, Suncrest needs to understand who owns what during an incident. We have regulatory obligations to be able to show recovery times and chain of custody for logs.
[00:45] Priya: Absolutely. We built the BCDR doc to map responsibilities across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For hosted, Redwood manages the control plane and infra; we provide runbooks and post-incident reports. For Dedicated, you get reserved pools - we still operate the runtime but there's a handshake on network access and maintenance windows. For Private, full customer control so you'll own recovery execution.

[01:10] Lara: Can you be specific about RTO/RPO numbers? We need numbers for our third-party risk team.
[01:16] Priya: Sure. Typical production profile: Hosted API aiming for RTO of 4 hours for major outages, RPO near zero for the model-serving layer thanks to KV cache and persistent state avoidance; but for catastrophic region failure we designate RPO of up to 15 minutes depending on replication policy. For Dedicated, we can get RTO down to 30-60 minutes if you opt into cross-zone replicas and standby pools. For Private on-prem it's variable - depends on your infra, but our recommended runbooks get you sub-1h RTO if you follow the template.
[01:50] Mark: 4 hours hosted is... borderline for us. Which parts take the longest?
[01:54] Priya: The slowest bits are control-plane failovers and activating cross-region model caches. Model weights are stored in object storage; pulling and warming takes time unless you keep hot replicas. Also network reconfiguration when IPs or peering changes - that's why Dedicated standby pools help.

[02:20] Daniel: On RPO, how do you ensure no customer data is lost? For example transient prompts or logs - retention and replication details?
[02:29] Priya: Good question - by design we avoid writing customer request payloads to durable storage except for audit logs and (opt-in) request logging for debugging. Audit logs are replicated and append-only; for hosted we retain logs 90 days by default, with options for longer retention. We can ship logs to your SIEM via syslog/ACL or to your S3 with encryption.
[02:55] Mark: Is that configurable per-account? We can't have sensitive prompts leaving our vault.
[02:59] Alex: Yes - you can opt out of request logging and only keep metadata/trace IDs. If you require complete data isolation, Dedicated or Private is recommended, plus customer-managed KMS.

[03:20] Lara: KMS - can you outline the options? We need to know whether Redwood ever has access to plaintext keys.
[03:28] Priya: We support three modes: Redwood-managed KMS (default), customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. In customer-managed mode, keys are in your account and Redwood only gets wrapped keys - we never get plaintext. HSM/private deploys eliminate vendor access entirely.
[03:50] Mark: Good. We'll want customer-managed keys and proof that you don't cache plaintext.
[03:54] Priya: We don't cache plaintext; keys are used to unwrap per-session encryption material which is ephemeral. We can walk through the KMS integration doc.

[04:10] Samir: Quick note - we'll include the KMS diagram in the post-call package.

[04:20] Mark: SLA and credits? We've seen banks push for 99.99% and clear credit formulas.
[04:26] Alex: Our standard enterprise SLA for Dedicated is 99.95% with defined credit tiers; for Hosted there is a managed SLA option you can buy up to 99.9%. For Private we negotiate. Credits are prorated monthly, and we have clear definitions for downtime windows and excluded events (force majeure, scheduled maintenance with notice).
[04:50] Lara: If we have a P1, what's the escalation sequence? We need names and target response times.
[04:56] Priya: Our standard P1 path: 15-minute initial response from on-call, 30-minute triage with SE involvement, and 1-hour engagement from engineering in case of systemic issues. Escalation to an on-call engineering manager at 2 hours, and a post-incident review within 72 hours. We can provide a contact matrix with phone and pager.
[05:20] Daniel: Are those targets contractual or best-effort? We need them contractual for our procurement.
[05:25] Alex: For Dedicated, those are contractual in the enterprise SLA. For Hosted it's part of the managed SLA upgrade. We'll include the exact Service Level Attachment in the contract.

[05:40] Mark: What about communications during incidents - status page, customer notifications?
[05:44] Priya: We have a public status page for broad outages and a private incident channel for customers in enterprise tiers. During a P1 you get initial notification within 30 minutes, updates every 60 minutes until resolved, and a post-mortem.

[06:10] Lara: Post-mortem sensitivity - sometimes we need redacted versions for regulators. Can you provide different tiers?
[06:15] Priya: Yes, we can provide redacted reports and a regulator-facing summary. Audit logs of actions taken can be made available in read-only exports.

[06:30] Mark: How are audit logs protected from tampering? We need tamper-evidence and chain-of-custody.
[06:36] Priya: Logs are write-once, append-only with versioning in object storage; we also maintain immutability via signed digests and optional push to customer-owned storage. We support log streaming to your SIEM which you control, and can provide signed checksums for tamper-evidence.

[07:00] Daniel: Do you support pushing logs to Splunk/Datadog?
[07:04] Priya: Yes - Splunk, Datadog, S3, and syslog endpoints - with TLS and mutual auth where needed.

[07:20] Mark: Walk me through a hypothetical incident: model-serving node caught fire, region degraded, what's the sequence?
[07:27] Priya: Step 1 immediate detection: automated health checks and our runtime alerting; Step 2 failover to standby pool or alternative region depending on policy; Step 3 notify customers via private incident channel; Step 4 root cause analysis, then restore from hot replicas or rehydrate weights from object store into warmed hosts. If cross-region failover is needed and you elected to keep hot replicas, RTO is faster; otherwise rehydrate time is the main bottleneck.

[08:00] Lara: For the rehydrate process, how long to pull a 20GB model?
[08:04] Priya: Depends on bandwidth - typical 20GB pull and warm is 10-20 minutes on fast networks, but decryption + kernel initialization can add more. That's why we recommend partial prewarm for critical endpoints.

[08:28] Alex: Note - sometimes the transcript has minor ASR weirdness here, e.g., 'caught fire' might be a figure of speech.

[08:40] Mark: Can we run an RTO drill? We want a scripted test with injected failure and measured times.
[08:45] Priya: Yes - we offer runbook templates and we can run a joint drill during the Dedicated trial. We'll measure detection, failover, and end-to-end recovery times and produce a metric pack.

[09:05] Daniel: Who signs off? Our ops and security both need to be present.
[09:08] Priya: We recommend a 2-hour scheduled drill: Redwood SE, your infra and security leads, and the network team. We'll run the scenario and capture logs + screenshots for auditors.

[09:28] Lara: About escalation contacts - we need a phone and a SAML-backed chat channel integration.
[09:34] Samir: We support SAML SSO and can integrate with your enterprise Slack workspace for incident notifications; for phone/pager we can add escalation numbers into the SLA contact matrix.

[09:50] Mark: On SSO and RBAC, how granular is the role model? We need separation of duties: deploy vs ops vs billing.
[09:57] Priya: RBAC is role-based with custom roles: Admin, Deployer, Operator, Auditor, Billing. You can map via SCIM groups from your IdP and we support enforced SSO for enterprise.

[10:20] Lara: Audit trail for actions in the console - who did what and when?
[10:24] Priya: All console actions are logged with actor, IP, timestamp, and a diff for config changes. Those logs are part of the audit export and can be retained longer on request.

[10:40] Daniel: Any known limitation in hybrid Private setups? We have a legacy HSM that requires specific drivers.
[10:47] Priya: For custom HSMs we usually validate in a prep phase; some drivers require a small agent on-prem. We can run compatibility tests as part of onboarding.

[11:05] Mark: Let's talk about the chain-of-command during a regulatory audit after an incident. We want a named Redwood liaison who can testify or provide documentation.
[11:12] Alex: We'll assign a technical account manager and a security liaison for the statement of facts; we also provide PS hours for audit support.

[11:25] Lara: Is there a play for rolling back to a previous model version if a new model behaves badly mid-run?
[11:30] Priya: Yes - rollouts support canary and instant rollback to pinned model versions; we log the rollout change and can automate rollback on quality gates.

[11:46] Daniel: For the dedicated trial, we want to validate RPO with simulated writes and then observe whether any requests are lost when failing over.
[11:54] Priya: We'll instrument unique request IDs and show end-to-end tracing so you can verify no loss or surface gaps. We'll also supply a script to generate load and correlate traces with our logs.

[12:18] Mark: About SLAs for uptime credits - what is the maximum credit? We need to map to our vendor policy.

[12:24] Alex: Credits scale with downtime percentage; max credit is typically up to 50% of monthly service fees for extreme breaches per our contract templates. We'll provide the precise SLM attachment.

[12:40] Lara: On-call rotation disclosure - we don't want personal numbers circulating. Can contacts be role addresses (pager/team) rather than personal?
[12:47] Samir: Yes, we provide role-based pages and a primary escalation alias. Personal numbers are only included with consent.

[13:00] Daniel: Any prior incidents you can share as references (sanitized)? We're especially interested in cross-region failover experience.
[13:08] Priya: We have anonymized post-mortems for 2025-11 outage and a 2025-08 degradation incident; we'll include links in the follow-up. They show detection-to-recovery timelines and lessons learned.

[13:30] Mark: Great. A few nitpicks from procurement: we need SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 attestation, data residency statement for EU and US, and proof of penetration testing cadence.
[13:43] Alex: We'll attach SOC 2 and ISO, and a data residency doc. We run pentests quarterly and can share summary reports under NDA.

[14:00] Lara: For data residency, does Hosted allow region pinning? We need US-only processing for some workloads.
[14:06] Priya: Yes, you can pin workloads to regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. Hosted supports region controls but some control-plane functions may be in a central region depending on the plan - we'll clarify in writing.

[14:28] Mark: My last concern - time to escalate to execs for regulatory-sensitive incidents. We need guaranteed notification to our CISO and privacy officer within 1 hour if data residency is impacted.
[14:38] Alex: That can be added as a contract clause for Dedicated customers; we'll include a guaranteed notification SLA and escalation to our executive on-call if certain impact thresholds are met.

[14:55] Lara: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[15:00] Alex: Recap - Redwood to send SOC 2 + ISO docs, KMS architecture diagram, sample SLA attachment, and redacted post-mortems. Redwood to provision Dedicated trial and propose dates for RTO drill. Suncrest to share on-call rota and decision on customer-managed KMS.

[15:18] Mark: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[15:21] Daniel: None from me.
[15:22] Lara: All good.
[15:25] Alex: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the packet by Thursday.
[15:28] Samir: I'll send calendar invites for the drill options.
[15:31] Mark: Thanks.

[END]
